title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 5.99 (versions follow prime numbers; 599 after 593): she weaves her own sentence. In v5.93 the words that came out of the rule of places chose, in her books, the sentence that said most. Now they are only the index: with them she finds the six sentences that hold most of them, and those sentences, and nothing else, go to her school's song (what two of them say is a rule), which sings a sentence written in none of her books. The loose words do not go to the song: a loose word brings no order. With no rule sung, the sentence of most clues as it is. Seen in a hidden copy, four questions: asked what the genome is she wove a sentence of her own that is nearly a definition, with the wrong subject; asked what a cell is, a tangle of words. She weaves unevenly, and there is no measure yet of how often she weaves well. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v5.57: Luma purificada. Prototipo de investigación.
